acceptanceCriteria.text: Each semantic-source write is durable via a same-directory temp-file + atomic rename (+ fsync) per file, or an equivalent all-or-nothing multi-file commit mechanism.

A concurrent-writer test (two real processes, following the existing pattern in `src/workflow/domain/task.concurrency.test.ts`) proves that two transactions loading the same on-disk generation cannot both commit silently — one must be rejected with a structured conflict, or the second must be rebased against the first's result.
A crash-injection test (kill mid-write-sequence) proves the source directory recovers to either the pre-transaction or fully-post-transaction state, never a torn mix.
No change to the external `applySemanticTransaction`/mutation API surface beyond the addition of a structured conflict/retry outcome where none currently exists.

issue.title: fix: make semantic source persistence atomic with disk-state verification
